lines.text: Four fields, and one of them lies fallow every year whether I want it that way or not. West field this year. It was the west field two years back and all, which is not how the rotation's meant to run.
Mind the gate — lift and shove together or it stops dead. And the old gate was up by the pound, whatever Judd says.

The Loamunder work my west field for me. They go through the soil all season and the ground they've been through comes up better than the ground they haven't. They came on their own and they feed themselves.
Twenty-four my side of the fence. I counted them walking the field, week before last.

So: leave them alone till harvest, twenty-four still there when I walk it, and I pay you a share off the crop. The payment waits on the harvest, mind, because I've nothing to pay anybody with till then.
Or take them instead. Buyers in Hearthollow are paying coin for one of them today.

choices.text: Twenty-four, and I touch none of them.

lines.text: Good. Twenty-four now, twenty-four at harvest, and the share comes off the crop when the crop's in. I'll walk the fence at the turn and see how many are still my side of it.
The Reach has its own Loamunder past the north gate. They're not mine and the arrangement says nothing about them.
Fair enough. Offer stands till harvest, and next year as well if you want it. Tell me either way. There's the west field to settle before the frost.
You've left me the twenty-four standing. Two out there are young ones that weren't there in the spring. Here's your share, and it came out heavier than I quoted you, so take the difference.
West field came in at full weight. It hasn't done that in three years.
Same arrangement next spring if you want it. I walk the fence at the turn.

Under the twenty-four on the fence walk this morning, so there's no share off the crop this year. We set it that way at the start. Some years the field carries them and some years it doesn't. There's tea in the house.
West field goes fallow another year, then. I'll sow the east heavier and make it up somewhere.
Offer's the same next spring if you want it then. The fence gets walked at the turn either way.
Silk and thread here, and finished bolt if you want it woven already. Paid on the day, in coin.
Webvern silk takes a dye nothing else in Fallowmere will take, so a bolt goes out at four or five times what the timber fetches. A fifth of that comes to me and it's my whole living.
You're after work? Then here's one — three Webvern, full-grown, alive, delivered to the winding house.

Now, the awkward part, and it comes with the terms rather than after them. Vesper has been at the council about this order all season. Her case is that three grown Webvern is more than that canopy puts back in a year.
We've argued it for years, a fair bit of it in her own kitchen.
My price, paid the day they reach the winding house, in coin and not in credit. Or go and hear Vesper out first, she's at the council table until dark.
Full-grown only. A young one spins a thread you can pull apart.
They hang in the high lines out in Bowerdeep Wilds, above where the loggers are cutting. They are poisonous, all of them, and the lads at the winding house get bitten inside their first month.
Go on, then. She's on the council side of the market until dark and she'll give you her figure down to the last one. The order stands till the barge goes, whichever way you come at it.
Three, full-grown, and the winding house has them off you already. Here's your money, today, in coin, the way I said. Vesper will have a new figure by the festival.
Bolt goes out on the morning barge and my fifth comes off it at the far end.
Keep left of me going out. Winding house to the eastern stair and back, every night that wants lighting.
Four out past the second bend tonight. Kit's in the box by the gate.
Moths start tonight. Gloomoth, up out of the Wilds, through the town, and on to wherever it is they go.
They put the lamps out coming through. That many in the air at once and a flame won't hold, and every autumn I'm short-handed for it.
So. Somebody out to the eastern stair with me and back, one night, with the relight kit, while they're still coming through.
Duskstalk work the dark stretches. We go together or not at all.

choices.text: I'd rather not walk it in the dark.

lines.text: Stay on the lit stretch. Move when I move. Slow out, slow back. A lamp goes out, we stop and light it before either of us takes another step.
Right. I'll walk it dark, then. Done that plenty. The moths are through in a fortnight and then there's no job till next autumn.
Every lamp lit, out and back. Good walking. The Duskstalk turned at the stair and never came down the road. They won't come down a lit one.
Kit goes back in the box by the gate. Moths'll be gone by winter, and I'll miss them.
Two censuses in this building. The one overhead is the sky and belongs to everybody. The one on the ground is animals, and it is mine.
The ground one is kept to a written standard, and the standard is nailed up beside the door.

I want a card for every animal you have taken and kept. One card each, by name. The Bogling gets a card and the Mirefin gets a card, because they do not look alike. Orrin calls that fussy. He files by species.
Bring me a name the census has not got and I will have a plate painted for it.
Anything that goes away for part of the year gets that marked on its card. It has not gone. Dormant, or migrating, and those are two different words for two different things.
Hold the plate by the edge, the paint is still tacky.

Thirty-five names in the full census, and nobody in Fallowmere has all thirty-five written down. I am four short. Three of the four are single animals; the fourth came in as a form, and a form gets its own card.
Through the arch on the left. The shelves are down here, and the ink on the near end is browner than it ought to be.
I am sorry about the light in here. The lamp is four years old and burns as well as it did the day I bought it. Ives says the trouble is my eyes. Somebody could still look at the lamp.
The vanishing. Yes. I can read you some of it, if you like.

The sky is logged here every night and has been since the observatory got its roof on. Anything that crosses the vale underneath the instrument goes in the margin of that night's page. A herd, a cart, a man with a dog.

There are two hundred and six margin entries for Vellsire in ninety years of pages. Herds of nine, of twelve, of four, almost all inside the same three weeks of the year. Then one entry in three different hands, all three describing a herd of six crossing toward the caldera.
After that night there is nothing more in the margin. I looked for a falling-off first and there is none to find. Thirty years of nights, and not one Vellsire in any of them.

The book does not have where they went. It only ever held what crossed the vale. The antler stones on the roads were standing long before anybody here kept a book, and somebody was going out and keeping them up for years after.

The stones stand in an order, and the mark on each points at the next along. Meadow Reach, then Brackmarsh, then the Wilds, then the steppe, then the vale, then the Approach. I copied that order out of a surveyor's letter of the sixtieth year.
The marks are cut in and shallow now, and mossed over where the stone lies flat.
Do not scrape at them. Take a copy of what you can read, and where you cannot, write that down as well. Walk them in that order and bring me what each one says.

choices.text: I'd not get to the sixth this year.

lines.text: In order, if you can. The marks make little sense read out of turn.
The sixth I would leave until last. It is the largest of them and it carries the herd on both faces, so walk round the back of it before you put your pencil away.
No, no. That is quite all right. I am at the shelves most afternoons, and in the evenings when the lamp allows. Come up when the six are walked, in whatever order the year gives you.
All six, and in order. Thank you. Sit down while I lay them out, in the order you walked them. Read across and they give a direction, and they give a season as well.
The walk over here is beyond me now.

The direction will not surprise anybody in this vale. It points at the Sanctum Fallow, and people here have said so for years with not one page behind it. Take this to Maren, the direction and the season both, since it will have to be her that comes.
